# Methodology and reproducibility

This gallery contains **original synthetic data and original R figures**. It
demonstrates four foundational graph purposes: separated categorical bars,
numeric distribution, location/spread summaries, and uncertainty of a resampled
*estimator*. It does not reproduce source textbook figures or study data.
Source edition/section evidence is recorded in
[Graph method alignment](GRAPH_METHODS_ALIGNMENT.md) and bibliographic credits
in the central source register.

Every figure distinguishes observations from estimates, includes a denominator,
labels measurements with units, and identifies the type of quartiles or interval
where relevant. Mean markers, box whiskers, individual observations, and
confidence limits must never be conflated.

```{r graph-setup}
required <- c("ggplot2", "knitr")
missing <- required[!vapply(required, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly=TRUE)]
if (length(missing)) stop("Missing graph dependencies: ", paste(missing,collapse=", "))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=TRUE)
module_candidates <- c("06_RESOURCES/R/biostat_graphs.R",
                       "../../06_RESOURCES/R/biostat_graphs.R")
modules <- module_candidates[file.exists(module_candidates)]
if (!length(modules)) stop("Cannot locate original biomedical graph module.")
source(modules[1], local=TRUE)
set.seed(params$seed)
synthetic <- data.frame(
  subject_id = sprintf("S%03d", seq_len(48L)),
  subtype = factor(rep(c("Luminal-like","Basal-like"),each=24L),
                   levels=c("Luminal-like","Basal-like")),
  grade = factor(sample(c("I","II","III"),48L,replace=TRUE,
                        prob=c(.2,.5,.3)),levels=c("I","II","III")),
  marker = c(stats::rnorm(24L,12,2),stats::rnorm(24L,9,3))
)
synthetic$marker[c(5L,39L)] <- NA_real_
stopifnot(nrow(synthetic)==48L,!anyDuplicated(synthetic$subject_id),
          sum(is.na(synthetic$marker))==2L)
```

# 1. Separated categorical bar graph

```{r graph-bars, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.6}
p_bar <- biostat_graph_bar(synthetic,category="grade",
  title="Synthetic tumor-grade frequencies")
print(p_bar)
knitr::kable(attr(p_bar,"figure_statistics"),
             caption="Exact grade counts; total denominator is 48")
```

Separate bars represent mutually exclusive categories. The vertical axis is a
count rather than a mean or percentage. Numeric label frequencies and total N
are available independently of the figure.

# 2. Continuous distribution histogram

```{r graph-distribution, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.7}
observed <- synthetic$marker[!is.na(synthetic$marker)]
p_hist <- ggplot2::ggplot(data.frame(marker=observed),
                         ggplot2::aes(x=.data$marker)) +
  ggplot2::geom_histogram(bins=15L,fill="#0072B2",colour="white") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title="Synthetic marker distribution",
    subtitle=sprintf("Observed n=%d; missing=%d",
                     length(observed),sum(is.na(synthetic$marker))),
    x="Fictional marker (arbitrary teaching score)",
    y="Number of observations",
    caption="Histogram bars show frequency intervals, not categorical groups."
  ) + ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size=12)
print(p_hist)
```

A histogram shows the shape of a numeric variable. Adjacent intervals are not
separate categories; use an appropriate fixed bin policy for comparisons.

# 3. Median, quartiles, mean, whiskers and observations

```{r graph-box, fig.width=8, fig.height=5.2}
pal <- c("Luminal-like"="#0072B2","Basal-like"="#D55E00")
p_box <- biostat_graph_box(
  synthetic,value="marker",group="subtype",
  unit="arbitrary teaching score",palette=pal,
  title="Synthetic marker by fictional subtype"
)
print(p_box)
knitr::kable(attr(p_box,"figure_statistics"),
             caption="Unrounded type-2 quartiles, mean, 1.5×IQR whiskers and denominators")
```

The box spans Q1–Q3 with a distinct median line. The **+** signifies the
sample mean, not the midpoint of the box or a confidence limit. Whiskers are
observed extrema within 1.5×IQR; outlying observations remain visible as
separate points. These figures use **type-2** R quantiles explicitly. Never
silently substitute another quantile convention in an existing study.

# 4. Stem-and-leaf: individual observed values

```{r graph-stem, results='markup'}
## Display a small subset so the textual stem-and-leaf remains readable.
stem_text <- biostat_graph_stem(
  round(synthetic$marker[seq_len(16L)],1),
  unit="arbitrary teaching score"
)
cat(paste(stem_text,collapse="\n"))
```

Stem-and-leaf is a textual distribution display for modest sample sizes. It
retains digit-level observation information at the chosen display precision;
the data's unit and the deliberate pre-display rounding are recorded.

# 5. Resampling distribution and percentile interval

```{r graph-bootstrap, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.8}
## Independent synthetic subjects are the resampling unit.
groups <- split(synthetic$marker,synthetic$subtype)
left <- groups[["Luminal-like"]]
right <- groups[["Basal-like"]]
left <- left[!is.na(left)];right <- right[!is.na(right)]
observed_difference <- mean(right)-mean(left)
boot <- replicate(1000L,
  mean(sample(right,length(right),replace=TRUE))-
  mean(sample(left,length(left),replace=TRUE))
)
p_boot <- biostat_graph_bootstrap(
  boot,estimate=observed_difference,unit="score difference",
  title="Bootstrap distribution of synthetic group mean differences"
)
print(p_boot)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  resamples=length(boot),point_estimate=observed_difference,
  lower=unname(stats::quantile(boot,.025,type=7)),
  upper=unname(stats::quantile(boot,.975,type=7))),
  caption="Point estimate and percentile bootstrap limits (display rounding only)")
```

This histogram describes **1000 resampled mean differences**, not the original
individual measurements. The vertical markers distinguish point estimate,
lower percentile and upper percentile. Valid uncertainty statements require
correct resampling units and appropriate interval assumptions.

# Acceptance boundaries

- All records and values are simulated. Nothing is a breast cancer effect
  estimate, verified assay distribution or clinical risk.
- Graphics demonstrate different questions and therefore use different axes
  and denominators intentionally.
- A generated figure is not accepted until the R chunks execute and the
  rendered HTML is visually inspected for labels, legend placement and clipping.
